claim.claim-text: 1. A carbon fiber package which is a fiber package in which a continuous carbon fiber bundle is traverse-wound on a bobbin,
wherein the continuous carbon fiber bundle is partially split into sub-bundles, and a width of the continuous carbon fiber bundle is smaller than a total sum of widths of the sub-bundles.

2. A carbon fiber package which is a fiber package in which a continuous carbon fiber bundle is traverse-wound on a bobbin, wherein the continuous carbon fiber bundle is partially split into sub-bundles and is wound on the bobbin so that the sub-bundles overlap each other.
3. The carbon fiber package according to Claim 1 or 2, wherein the width of the continuous carbon fiber bundle is 90% of the total sum of the widths of the sub-bundles or less.
4. The carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 1 to 3, wherein the continuous carbon fiber bundle is partially split into three or more sub-bundles.
5. The carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 1 to 4, wherein a filament number of the sub-bundle is 5K or less.
6. The carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 1 to 5, wherein a total filament number of the continuous carbon fiber bundle is 12K or more.
7. The carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 1 to 6, wherein the carbon fiber package is a square end type package.
8. The carbon fiber package according to Claim 7, wherein a winding ratio is not an integer.
9. The carbon fiber package according to Claim 8, a fraction of the winding ratio after a decimal point is a multiple of none of 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 and 1/5.
10. The carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 7 to 9, wherein a lead angle at a start of winding is 5° to 30° and the lead angle at an end of winding is 2° to 17°.
11. A manufacturing method of a sheet molding compound comprising using the carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 1 to 9.
12. Use of the carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 1 to 9 in manufacturing a sheet molding compound.
13. A manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package in which a continuous carbon fiber bundle is traverse-wound on a bobbin, comprising

a splitting step of partially splitting a continuous carbon fiber bundle into sub-bundles and a winding step of winding the continuous carbon fiber bundle partially split into the sub-bundles on a bobbin, wherein in the winding step, the continuous carbon fiber bundle is wound on the bobbin so that a width of the continuous carbon fiber bundle is smaller than a total sum of widths of the sub-bundles.
14. A manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package in which a continuous carbon fiber bundle is traverse-wound on a bobbin, comprising

a splitting step of partially splitting a continuous carbon fiber bundle into sub-bundles and a winding step of winding the continuous carbon fiber bundle partially split into the sub-bundles on a bobbin, wherein in the winding step, the continuous carbon fiber bundle is wound on the bobbin so that the sub-bundles overlap each other.

15. The manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package according to Claim 13 or 14, wherein in the winding step, the continuous carbon fiber bundle is wound on the bobbin so that the width of the continuous carbon fiber bundle is 90% of the total sum of the widths of the sub-bundles or less.

16. The manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 13 to 15, wherein in the splitting step, the continuous carbon fiber bundle is partially split into three or more sub-bundles.
17. The manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 13 to 16, wherein a filament number of the sub-bundle is 5K or less.
18. The manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 13 to 17, wherein a total filament number of the continuous carbon fiber bundle is 12K or more.
19. The manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 13 to 18, wherein the fiber package is a square end type package.
20. The manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package according to Claim 19, wherein a winding ratio is not an integer in the winding step.

21. The manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package according to Claim 20, wherein a fraction of the winding ratio after a decimal point is a multiple of none of 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 and 1/5 in the winding step.

22. The manufacturing method of a carbon fiber package according to any one of Claims 19 to 21, wherein in the winding step, a lead angle at a start of winding is 5° to 30° and the lead angle at an end of winding is 2° to 17°.
